subject: ACME staging load rehearsal & acceptance checklist
messages:
From: Tom Bauer <tbauer@acmeretail.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Siena Lopez <slopez@acmeretail.com>
Date: 2026-09-07T16:12:00Z
Subject: ACME staging load rehearsal & acceptance checklist

Hi Mina / Mina's team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. We'd like to run a staged dry run in your staging environment next week to validate our acceptance criteria before we schedule production cutover. High level targets we've agreed on internally:
- Sustained throughput: 250 requests/sec (expected average prompt length ~600 tokens)
- P95 latency target: < 180 ms (end-to-end, token emit)
- Tail latency (99th): ideally < 400 ms, acceptable up to 550 ms for short spikes
- Successful completion rate: >= 99.8% (no server errors during the run)

Can you confirm whether Redwood can run a 30-minute soak at 200 req/s followed by two 10-minute spike windows (400 req/s) in staging? Also: will you produce a CSV with per-request latencies and a simple artifacts bundle (telemetry + KV cache hit rates)?

Proposed windows (PST): Tue 2026-09-09 09:00-11:00 or Wed 2026-09-10 10:00-12:00. We prefer Tue if possible.

Siena and I will coordinate client-side ramps and provide the exact prompt corpus. Let us know what we need to open (IPs/ports), and any test client config you prefer.

Thanks,
Tom Bauer
Head of Platform Operations
Acme Retail

[Attachment: onboarding-acceptance-draft.xlsx (XLSX) referenced]

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Bauer <tbauer@acmeretail.com>, Siena Lopez <slopez@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-07T18:03:00Z
Subject: Re: ACME staging load rehearsal & acceptance checklist

Thanks Tom — we can run the rehearsal in staging. I've attached a short load plan that maps your targets to Redwood test phases (soak, spike, and recovery) and lists the telemetry artifacts we'll share. High-level notes:
- We will provision a dedicated staging pool for the rehearsal (no other tenants) to keep noise low.
- Test phases: 10m warmup @ 100 r/s -> 30m soak @ 200 r/s -> 2x 10m spikes @ 400 r/s separated by 5m recovery.
- Measurement: p50/p95/p99 latencies, per-request success code, model token counts, KV cache hit ratio, GPU util and queue depth sampling at 1s resolution.
- Acceptance criteria: p95 < 180 ms AND success rate >= 99.8% for the soak. We will flag any sustained quota or queuing events.

Action items for Tue 2026-09-09 09:00 PST run (assuming this window works):
1) Acme: provide the prompt corpus (CSV), client ramp script, and list of source IPs for whitelisting — due Mon EOD.
2) Redwood (me/Monica/Karthik): provision staging pool, prepare telemetry store and Drive folder for artifacts, validate client connectivity — by Mon EOD.
3) Post-run: we will share a artifacts bundle with per-request CSV + summarized dashboard and a short run write-up within 24 hours.

I've attached the plan (acme-staging-loadplan-20260907.pdf). Monica, Karthik — can you confirm the measurement hooks and whether the 1s sampling for GPU/util is sufficient?

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Quick internal note / suggested test tweaks — tagging Tom for visibility but this is primarily infra prep: 

- Telemetry: we'll emit per-request latency in ms plus a request-id to correlate. We'll produce the CSV (columns: ts, req_id, r_lat_ms, token_count, status_code, kv_hit) as requested.
- Sampling: 1s GPU/util is fine; add 250ms queue-depth probe to better catch micro-bursts.
- Ramp scripts: recommend 90s linear ramp to soak point (200 r/s) rather than immediate jump; this reduces false positives on queueing. We'll mirror that on client side if they agree.
- Failure modes: if error rate > 0.2% sustained over a 2-minute window we will halt and capture heap traces / kernel logs and escalate.

Proposed internal timeline for Tue run:
- 08:15 UTC: final staging pool smoke and connectivity test
- 08:45 UTC: prompt corpus upload to test bucket + client whitelisting check
- 09:00 UTC: warmup -> soak -> spikes -> cool down (approx 50 minutes total)
- 10:00 UTC: artifacts collection + initial pass at CSV prep
- 10:30 UTC: initial readout to Acme

I'll prepare the test harness and a small README for how we generated the CSV.

-Monica
Sr. Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Bauer <tbauer@acmeretail.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-10T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: ACME staging load rehearsal & acceptance checklist — results

Hi all — run completed Tue 2026-09-09 09:00 PST (we kept your client ramps). Summary and artifacts attached. Short readout:

- Soak (30m @ 200 r/s): p50=42 ms, p95=162 ms, p99=355 ms, success rate=99.93% -> PASS vs soak acceptance (p95 < 180 ms; success >= 99.8%).
- Spikes (2x10m @ 400 r/s): first spike p95=210 ms (exceeded 180), p99=620 ms (spiky tail); second spike similar but slightly improved after cache warm. We observed short-lived queuing during spike ramps corresponding to 3x queue depth increase for ~45s.
- Observations: KV cache miss rate decreased from 18% at start to 6% mid-soak; warm cache materially helps p95. GPU utilization peaked at 88% during spikes; no OOMs or kernel failures.

Artifacts shared: load-results-20260909.csv (per-request latencies + status), run-dashboard-snapshot.png, staging-kernel-logs.tar.gz (link in Drive). Full bundle uploaded to the Drive folder below.

Recommendation / next steps:
1) For production acceptance we recommend a brief pre-warm period (5-10 minutes of low traffic) to reduce KV miss tail behavior.
2) If Acme expects repeated, sustained 400 r/s spikes in prod, we should discuss a dedicated higher-concurrency pool or a short autoscale buffer.
3) We'll open a short follow-up meeting to review the CSV and walk through the p99 traces — propose Wed 2026-09-11 09:00 PST.

Tom, Siena — please confirm whether you want us to run an additional spike window with a longer pre-warm (10m) or proceed to production cutover planning.

Attachments: load-results-20260909.csv
